correctness.rationale: The leaf-attachment recursion enumerates every unlabelled tree up to nine vertices by induction, and canonical rooted-tree code comparison is an isomorphism test. The edge-split canonical invariant computes exact edge orbits, with the line-graph automorphism correspondence justified by Whitney and small-case checks. Census checks all 47 nine-vertex trees (and 1,1,1,2,3,6,11,23 smaller counts), uniquely identifying one gap. Independently, the eight-vertex line graph has explicit equitable quotient [[0,3],[1,1]] yet three true orbits of sizes 2,4,2. A second program tests all 8! permutations for its automorphisms and all eight one-vertex markings. Proof coverage is finite and exactly matches the claim; no finite tests are extrapolated to infinite classes.

value.rationale: The example gives a sharp minimal, uniquely characterized failure of a natural preservation conjecture: trees have particularly strong color refinement, but their line graphs need not have orbit-exact stable colors. The counterexample is structurally transparent through the equitable quotient versus triangle membership, and arbitrary one-vertex marking repairs it. Enumerating all first-order tree cases supplies a useful exact boundary test for counting-refinement preservation, beyond a contrived isolated negative experiment. No general uniqueness above order nine is claimed.
